engines.name: 4.0L twin-turbo V8 plug-in hybrid (AMG S63 E Performance)

issues.t: Air suspension (Airmatic) sagging overnight
issues.sym: One corner or one end of the car sits low after parking, the car is slow to rise after starting, a 'Car too low' or suspension warning appears, or the ride turns harsh and bouncy.
issues.why: The rubber air springs in the Airmatic struts crack and leak with age, usually after 60,000 to 100,000 miles. Torn dust boots let dirt in and speed this up, and the rear springs often go first. A faulty rear height sensor can also make the rear drop.
issues.next: Don't drive far if the car is sitting on its bump stops or a 'Stop vehicle' message shows. Have the leaking strut found with a leak test and replaced quickly, because a leak makes the compressor overwork and fail too.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor running constantly or burned out
issues.sym: A loud humming from behind the front bumper that runs a long time, the car taking ages to lift, or the car staying down with a 'Vehicle too low' warning.
issues.why: The compressor wears internally and can no longer build enough pressure. It usually fails early because a leaking air spring or valve block made it run far longer than it was designed to. A stuck relay can also keep it running until it burns out.
issues.next: Find and fix any air leak before or at the same time as replacing the compressor, or the new one will fail too. Ask the shop to replace the compressor relay as well.

issues.t: Active Body Control (ABC) hydraulic leak or pump failure
issues.sym: An ABC warning message, a corner that drops quickly, a hard or bouncy ride, too much body lean, red hydraulic fluid under the car, or a howl from the engine bay at low revs. Applies to S600, AMG and other cars ordered with ABC.
issues.why: The ABC system uses high-pressure hydraulic fluid instead of air. Its hoses and seals age, the pressure accumulators wear out after about 10 years or 60,000 miles, and neglected fluid wears the pump, valve blocks and struts.
issues.next: Stop and check the fluid level if a red ABC warning appears; driving with a burst hose can run the pump dry. Have a specialist read the ABC fault log and check the fluid condition before replacing parts.

issues.t: ABC suspension high-pressure hose can corrode and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Hydraulic fluid leaking near the front of the car, an ABC warning, or the car sinking and riding harshly.
issues.why: The steel inner layer of an ABC high-pressure hose could corrode from humidity and start leaking fluid. Mercedes recalled affected cars with Active Body Control to fit a corrosion-resistant hose.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to check your VIN for open recall work. If fluid is leaking, have the car towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Rust on body panels and subframe
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust on door bottoms, wheel arches, the trunk lid, or rust on the subframe underneath.
issues.why: Mercedes used a water-based paint and steel with weak corrosion protection in this era, and the body was not fully galvanized until early 2003. The 2007 to 2009 cars can also rust in salted-road areas; later cars are better protected.
issues.next: Have the underside and subframe inspected, especially before buying. Treat small spots early; structural rust on the subframe is a much bigger job.

issues.t: Power windows or door locks stop working
issues.sym: A window won't go up or down, moves slowly, or a door won't lock or unlock with the key fob, most often the driver's door.
issues.why: The heavy double-pane glass wears out window motors and regulators on older cars. Door control modules can corrode or fail internally, and lock actuators wear out.
issues.next: Have the door panel removed and the regulator, motor, lock actuator or door module tested. Some door module repairs need a Mercedes-level scan tool to code the new part.

issues.t: Central locking, trunk and seat functions fail (vacuum pump)
issues.sym: The central locking, trunk release, lumbar support, rear parking guide rods or heater flaps stop working, or a pump keeps buzzing in the trunk.
issues.why: One vacuum/pressure pump (the PSE pump) runs many comfort features on this generation. Its motor wears out and its hoses crack and leak.
issues.next: Have the PSE pump and its hoses tested for leaks. A leak can make the pump run until it fails, so fixing the hose early can save the pump.

issues.t: Broken coil spring or worn subframe bushings
issues.sym: A clunk over bumps, one corner sitting lower than the others, a harsh ride, or the car feeling loose and wandering.
issues.why: This is a very heavy car. Front springs can snap at the bottom and rear springs at the top, and the rubber subframe bushings wear out at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected on a lift. A broken spring can damage a tire, so replace it promptly; spring jobs on this car need proper spring compressors.

issues.t: Engine wiring harness insulation crumbling
issues.sym: Loss of power when pulling away, rough idle, stalling, misfires or a car that won't start.
issues.why: Engine harnesses built before January 1996 used insulation that breaks down with heat and age, letting wires short. Early 1996 cars may still have the old harness; Mercedes changed it during 1996 production.
issues.next: Ask whether the harness has been replaced. If not, have a mechanic inspect the wiring at the engine; replacing the harness is the lasting fix.

issues.t: Plastic camshaft oil tubes break
issues.sym: Ticking or clatter from the top of the engine, and in bad cases worn camshafts.
issues.why: The V8s spray oil onto the camshafts through plastic tubes (cam oilers) that turn brittle with heat and can break, starving the cam lobes of oil.
issues.next: Have the valve covers removed and the oil tubes checked. Owners recommend replacing them with metal versions.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak at the electrical plug
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping from the side of the transmission, low fluid, or erratic shifting and limp mode.
issues.why: The 5-speed automatic has an electrical connector that passes through the case. Its plastic adapter and O-rings harden and leak fluid.
issues.next: Have the connector adapter and seals replaced and the fluid topped up. This is a small part; don't ignore it, because low fluid damages the transmission.

issues.t: Sluggish shifts or torque converter shudder
issues.sym: Slow, lazy gear changes, a shudder at steady speed, or harsh shifts. Reverse may be the first gear to fail.
issues.why: The 5-speed automatic had no set fluid-change interval, so many have old, worn fluid. 2000 to 2002 cars in particular drew complaints about slow responses and converter shudder.
issues.next: Have the fluid and filter changed with the correct Mercedes fluid if there are no records, then recheck. If problems remain, get a transmission diagnosis before a rebuild.

issues.t: Crankshaft position sensor failure
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving, cranks but won't start (often when hot), or runs rough with a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor tells the engine computer when to fire. Heat breaks it down over time and it stops sending a signal.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The sensor is a common cause of no-starts on these cars.

issues.t: Water leaking into cabin or trunk
issues.sym: Wet carpets, water in the trunk spare-tire well, a damp smell, fogged windows, or electrical faults after rain.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog with debris and overflow, and taillight seals can let water into the trunk. Water then reaches modules and wiring.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains and check the taillight seals. Dry the carpets quickly and have any wet modules checked before they corrode.

issues.t: Blower motor regulator can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The fan stops working or a hot plastic or burning smell comes from the passenger footwell.
issues.why: A circuit defect in the blower motor regulator could make it overheat and melt or burn nearby parts. Mercedes recalled affected cars to replace it.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to confirm the recall was done. If you smell burning, turn the fan off and get it checked.

issues.t: V12 misfire from ignition coils or spark plugs
issues.eng: 5.8L V12 (S600), 5.5L twin-turbo V12 (S600), 6.0L twin-turbo V12 (S65 AMG, S600, Maybach)
issues.sym: Rough idle, shaking, misfires and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: The V12s have 24 spark plugs and coil packs that each fire six cylinders. These wear out, and the tight engine bay makes the work slow.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Don't drive long with a flashing check engine light, as unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converters.

issues.t: Worn timing idler gear (5.5L V8)
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft position or timing codes, rough running, or a rattle or ticking from the front of the engine.
issues.why: On early 5.5L V8 engines, a timing-drive idler gear made of too-soft metal wears its teeth, which upsets cam timing. A class-action settlement once extended coverage, but it has now expired for nearly all cars.
issues.next: Get the timing codes checked promptly. If the gear wears too far the chain can jump, which can damage the engine. The repair is big, so get a Mercedes specialist's quote.

issues.t: Transmission stuck in limp mode (conductor plate or control unit)
issues.sym: The transmission stops shifting and stays in one gear, with a warning message, often after a restart it works again for a while.
issues.why: The 7-speed automatic's electronics fail: the control unit, the conductor plate inside the valve body, or the valve body itself.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. A new control unit must be coded to the car; specialists can repair or reprogram units for less than the dealer.

issues.t: Climate blower motor stops working
issues.sym: The fan works only some of the time, then stops completely, so there is no air from the vents for A/C or heat.
issues.why: Moisture gets into the blower motor and it fails.
issues.next: Have the blower motor tested. Replacement takes up to about two hours.

issues.t: Hybrid inverter failure leaves car unable to start
issues.sym: The car won't start at all and shows hybrid system warnings.
issues.why: The inverter/converter that manages the hybrid system can fail. New parts are scarce.
issues.next: Have the hybrid system scanned by a dealer or hybrid specialist. On a high-mileage car, ask the shop whether the repair makes sense before going ahead.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start (twin-turbo V8)
issues.sym: A metallic rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, then possibly long cranking, misfires, power loss and a check engine light.
issues.why: Oil drains from the timing tensioner overnight, so the chain is briefly slack at start-up. Over time this stretches the chains and wears guides. Early production engines were affected most; Mercedes later revised parts.
issues.next: Don't ignore a cold-start rattle. Have a specialist check cam timing values; replacing tensioners early helps avoid a chain that jumps.

issues.t: Valve cover oil leak and burning oil smell
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, light smoke from the engine bay, or oil spots on the turbochargers.
issues.why: Heat warps the plastic valve covers so their gaskets no longer seal, and oil drips onto the hot turbos.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed. Replacing the valve covers, not only the gaskets, is usually needed. Oil on hot turbos is a fire risk, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Harsh or clunky gear changes
issues.sym: Hard upshifts or downshifts, especially between 2nd and 3rd gear.
issues.why: Worn transmission fluid or a conductor plate that has lost its calibration. Mercedes' long fluid interval leaves many cars with old fluid.
issues.next: Ask for any software updates, then a fluid and filter change with an adaptation reset. If that fails, the conductor plate may need replacing.

issues.t: Battery goes flat after the car sits
issues.sym: The battery is dead after a few days to a week parked, or the Mercedes app keeps sending low battery warnings.
issues.why: A control module, such as the infotainment, keyless entry or driver-assist units, fails to go to sleep and keeps drawing power.
issues.next: Have a shop measure the parked current draw to find the module that stays awake. Use a battery maintainer if the car sits for more than a week.

issues.t: Engine oil plugs may leak under high load (recall)
issues.sym: An oil leak, a burning oil smell or a low oil warning.
issues.why: Two engine oil plugs might not hold under high engine load. Leaking oil can reach hot parts and start a fire. Mercedes recalled S560s to add a retaining plate.
issues.next: Check that the recall was done using your VIN at nhtsa.gov or a dealer. Stop driving if you smell burning oil.

issues.t: Drive shaft joint can break (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration or clunking from under the car, or a sudden loss of drive power. Applies to 4MATIC all-wheel-drive S450 and S560 models.
issues.why: A universal joint in the drive shaft can break. Mercedes recalled affected 4MATIC cars to inspect and replace the drive shaft.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and book the free inspection. Pull over safely if you feel new vibration from under the car.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) may not work (recall)
issues.sym: An SOS or emergency call warning may show, or there may be no sign at all. After a crash the system might not call or might send the wrong location.
issues.why: Software problems in the communication module and its SIM card could disable the emergency call system or send an incorrect location. Mercedes fixed this with software updates.
issues.next: Make sure the software update was done, either over the air or at a dealer. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Engine may stall or overheat from Camtronic fault (recall)
issues.sym: An engine warning light, the engine overheating, or the engine suddenly stalling.
issues.why: If the Camtronic variable valve lift part fails mechanically, the engine computer software could react in a way that overheats or stalls the engine. A separate 2021 software recall also fixed a stalling fault on S580s.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a dealer confirm both software updates were done. If the engine warning light comes on, have it checked before long drives.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't restart.
issues.why: A nozzle on the fuel tank's suction jet pump could be loose or missing, which can make the fuel pump fail. Mercedes recalled 2021 S580s for this.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Front brake hoses can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: A brake fluid warning, a soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stopping distances, or fluid at a front wheel.
issues.why: The front brake hoses could rupture and leak brake fluid. Mercedes first recalled 2021 to 2023 cars and later expanded the recall to more S-Class models.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls. If the brake warning lights up or the pedal feels soft, stop and have the car towed.

issues.t: High-voltage starter generator unit can fail (recall)
issues.eng: 4.0L twin-turbo V8 plug-in hybrid (AMG S63 E Performance)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power with warning messages.
issues.why: A software error could make the control unit for the high-voltage starter alternator fail. Mercedes fixed it with a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the update done.

issues.t: Flush door handles don't respond or open on their own
issues.sym: The pop-out door handles don't extend when touched, are hard to pull, or open and close unexpectedly.
issues.why: Owners report the electric flush handles misbehave; the cause hasn't been pinned down publicly. Some found locking the car and walking away with the key stops it.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer under warranty and ask about software updates for the door control units.

issues.t: Clicking noise from dashboard
issues.sym: A clicking sound from the middle top of the dashboard or near the passenger seat, often when turning over uneven roads.
issues.why: Owners of newer cars report interior clicks that dealers have struggled to find. The cause isn't confirmed.
issues.next: Record the noise on your phone and show the dealer while the car is under warranty.
